cause_quote: The guest-privacy change made person Activity reads return FORBIDDEN and only added `if (error instanceof GatewayRequestError && error.gatewayCode === "FORBIDDEN") { currentResult = undefined; ... }`, leaving invalidate() to re-request the denied selection on every unrelated session change.
user_saw: A guest looking at a denied Activity view saw the permission error briefly replaced by loading placeholders whenever an unrelated session changed.
summary: Session activity now records a settled FORBIDDEN denial and skips unrelated invalidations and bucket refreshes for it, while retries, changed queries and authority changes (sharing/profile-identity, new hello) still reload.
reasoning: Person-Activity FORBIDDEN denials for guests were introduced by 5d3e157432a (#191978), whose UI part only cleared rows on FORBIDDEN and did not stop the existing invalidate/refresh paths from re-reading the denied query, so the flicker shipped with that feature. I confirmed the owner's history and the parent's invalidate() still refreshing on any session change; earlier refactors (10c95d1a605 etc.) predate the denial state, so they are not the cause.
